introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2024. Time allowed: three hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.
enonce_intro_markdown:
Copper has about $8.49\times10^{28}$ charge carriers per unit volume and a resistivity of $1.68\times10^{-8}\ \Omega\,\mathrm{m}$. In figure 2, a copper cable with a cross-sectional area of $0.27\ \mathrm{mm^2}$ is connected in series with a battery. The connecting cables have negligible resistance.

![fig-1](gce-al-physics-2024-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_2_fig_1.png)

figures.legende: Figure 2 : a battery and a switch in series with an ammeter A and a 752 cm length of copper cable; a voltmeter V is connected across the battery.

Question 2 : la charge élémentaire e = 1,60 x 10^-19 C est retenue (aucune feuille de données imprimée). La longueur du câble (752 cm = 7,52 m) est lue sur le schéma. Le voltmètre est lu comme branché aux bornes de la pile : sa lecture est la tension aux bornes, égale à R x I parce que les fils de connexion ont une résistance négligeable.

questions.corrige_markdown:
Take the elementary charge $e = 1.60\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$. The cable is $752\ \mathrm{cm} = 7.52\ \mathrm{m}$ long and $A = 0.27\ \mathrm{mm^2} = 0.27\times10^{-6}\ \mathrm{m^2}$.

**(i) Drift velocity.** The current is $I = nAve$, so
$$v = \frac{I}{nAe} = \frac{6.04}{8.49\times10^{28}\times0.27\times10^{-6}\times1.60\times10^{-19}} = 1.65\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}.$$
The drift velocity is about $1.65\ \mathrm{mm\,s^{-1}}$.

**(ii) Voltmeter reading.** Resistance of the cable:
$$R = \frac{\rho L}{A} = \frac{1.68\times10^{-8}\times7.52}{0.27\times10^{-6}} = 0.468\ \Omega.$$
The connecting cables have negligible resistance, so the voltmeter (across the battery) reads the p.d. across the cable:
$$V = IR = 6.04\times0.468 = 2.83\ \mathrm{V}.$$
**Voltmeter reading $\approx 2.83\ \mathrm{V}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Explain why the reading of the voltmeter increases when the switch is opened.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The battery has an internal resistance $r$. The voltmeter reads the **terminal p.d.** of the battery,
$$V = E - Ir.$$

- **Switch closed:** a current $I$ flows, so a p.d. $Ir$ (the "lost volts") is dropped across the internal resistance and the terminal p.d. is less than the e.m.f. $E$. Here $V = 2.83\ \mathrm{V}$.
- **Switch open:** the circuit is broken, so $I = 0$ (the voltmeter has a very high resistance and draws a negligible current). There are no lost volts, so the voltmeter reads the full e.m.f.: $V = E$.

Since $E > E - Ir$, the reading **increases** when the switch is opened. The e.m.f. is $E = 2.83 + 6.04\,r$ volts.
